title: Common Adverbs in Conversation: Amplifiers, Downtoners
titleZh: 对话中常见的副词：强化语与弱化语
credits: John Russell wrote this story for Learning English. George Grow was the editor.

sentences.en: From VOA Learning English, this is Everyday Grammar.
sentences.zh: 来自美国之音英语学习，这是日常语法。

sentences.en: Imagine you are at a business meeting.
sentences.zh: 想象你正在参加一场商务会议。

sentences.en: You have just presented a plan to your business partners.
sentences.zh: 你刚刚向你的商业伙伴展示了一份计划。

sentences.en: They want to give suggestions for how to make your plan better.
sentences.zh: 他们想就如何让你的计划更好提出建议。

sentences.en: The conversation might sound like this:
sentences.zh: 对话听起来可能像这样：

sentences.en: A: I really like your plan!
sentences.zh: A：我真的很喜欢你的计划！

sentences.en: B: Yes, it's pretty good … but it needs a little revising.
sentences.zh: B：是的，它相当好……但需要稍微修改一下。

sentences.en: A: Of course, you did a very good job.
sentences.zh: A：当然，你做得非常好。

sentences.en: But you might need to consider a few more points.
sentences.zh: 但你或许需要考虑更多几点。

sentences.en: B: Yes, it will probably be more effective if you highlight the staffing requirements and expand on the budget.
sentences.zh: B：是的，如果你强调人员配置需求并扩展预算，它可能会更有效。

sentences.en: Whether you like business or not, this conversation gives you important grammar information that you can use in just about any situation.
sentences.zh: 无论你是否喜欢商务活动，这段对话都为你提供了几乎在任何情况下都能使用的重要语法信息。

sentences.en: In particular, the exchange offers examples of some of the most important adverbs that you will hear in everyday speech.
sentences.zh: 特别是，这次交流提供了一些你在日常对话中最常听到的重要副词的示例。

sentences.en: This week, we will explore special adverbs that increase or decrease the force of a statement.
sentences.zh: 本周，我们将探索能够增强或减弱陈述力度的特殊副词。

sentences.en: These adverbs are sometimes called amplifiers or downtoners.*
sentences.zh: 这些副词有时被称为加强语或弱化语。

sentences.en: Adverbs are words that modify, or change, the meaning of adjectives, verbs, and sometimes entire sentences.
sentences.zh: 副词是修饰或改变形容词、动词以及有时整个句子意义的词。

sentences.en: They are often used to show time, a way of doing something, place, or degree – a measure of something.
sentences.zh: 它们常被用来表示时间、做某事的方式、地点或程度——即对某事物的衡量。

sentences.en: Some kinds of adverbs act as amplifiers.
sentences.zh: 有些种类的副词起到加强语的作用。

sentences.en: The word amplify means to make something stronger.
sentences.zh: 词amplify的意思是使某事物变得更强。

sentences.en: So these amplifiers make the meaning of an adjective or sentence stronger.
sentences.zh: 所以这些加强语使形容词或句子的意义更强。

sentences.en: In American English, amplifiers have three common uses: increasing intensity, expressing certainty and showing precision.
sentences.zh: 在美式英语中，加强语有三种常见用法：增强强度、表达确定性和显示精确性。

sentences.en: This information comes from Susan Conrad and Douglas Biber, two experts on English grammar.
sentences.zh: 这些信息来自苏珊·康拉德和道格拉斯·比伯，两位英语语法专家。

sentences.en: Words such as really and very are among the most common that increase the intensity of a statement.
sentences.zh: 像"really"和"very"这样的词，是增强语句强度的最常见词汇之一。

sentences.en: They usually modify an adjective.
sentences.zh: 它们通常修饰形容词。

sentences.en: Take the adjective good, for example.
sentences.zh: 以形容词"good"为例。

sentences.en: Imagine you are trying some food that your friends cooked.
sentences.zh: 想象你正在品尝朋友烹饪的食物。

sentences.en: Perhaps you want to tell them, "This food is good."
sentences.zh: 也许你想告诉他们："这食物很好。"

sentences.en: You could increase the intensity of your statement by using the word very:
sentences.zh: 你可以用"very"这个词来增强语句的强度：

sentences.en: "This food is very good."
sentences.zh: "这食物非常好。"

sentences.en: You could express certainty by using an amplifier such as definitely:
sentences.zh: 你可以用"definitely"这样的强化词来表达确定性：

sentences.en: "This is definitely the best food I've ever had."
sentences.zh: "这绝对是我吃过最好的食物。"

sentences.en: Or you could use an amplifier to show precision:
sentences.zh: 或者你可以用强化词来体现精确性：

sentences.en: "At exactly 5:13 p.m. on February 6th, I ate the best food I've ever had in my life!"
sentences.zh: "在2月6日下午5点13分，我吃了这辈子最好的食物！"

sentences.en: Other kinds of adverbs act as downtoners.
sentences.zh: 其他类型的副词起着弱化词的作用。

sentences.en: Downtoners are the opposite of amplifiers.
sentences.zh: 弱化词是强化词的反面。

sentences.en: They reduce the force of a statement or express doubt.
sentences.zh: 它们减弱语句的力度或表达怀疑。

sentences.en: In other words, they set the tone of a statement.
sentences.zh: 换句话说，它们为语句定下基调。

sentences.en: You can remember the term 'downtoner' by thinking about what it does: toning down a statement.
sentences.zh: 你可以通过思考弱化词的作用来记住"downtoner"这个术语：弱化语句。

sentences.en: Downtoners have three common functions: reducing intensity, expressing doubt or showing imprecision.
sentences.zh: 弱化词有三种常见功能：减弱强度、表达怀疑或体现不精确。

sentences.en: Three common downtoners in conversational English are pretty, maybe and probably, say Conrad and Biber.
sentences.zh: 康拉德和比伯说，英语对话中三种常见的弱化词是"pretty"、"maybe"和"probably"。

sentences.en: How can you use downtoners to change the meaning of the statement?
sentences.zh: 你如何使用弱化词来改变语句的含义？

sentences.en: Take our earlier example: "This food is good."
sentences.zh: 以我们之前的例子为例：“这道菜很好吃。”

sentences.en: If you wanted to reduce the intensity of your statement, you could say:
sentences.zh: 如果你想减弱语气，你可以这样说：

sentences.en: "This food is pretty good."
sentences.zh: “这道菜相当好吃。”

sentences.en: You could show doubt, even raise questions, by saying:
sentences.zh: 你也可以通过这样说表达怀疑，甚至提出疑问：

sentences.en: "This is maybe the best food I've ever had."
sentences.zh: “这可能是我吃过的最好的菜。”

sentences.en: Or,
sentences.zh: 或者，

sentences.en: "This is probably the best food I've ever had."
sentences.zh: “这大概是我吃过的最好的菜。”

sentences.en: These statements express someone’s opinion about the food.
sentences.zh: 这些句子表达了某人对食物的看法。

sentences.en: But they are not as strong as the example sentences that use amplifiers.
sentences.zh: 但它们不如使用强化词的句子那么有力度。

sentences.en: In other words, saying "This food is pretty good" is not as forceful as saying, "This food is really good."
sentences.zh: 换句话说，说“这道菜相当好吃”不如说“这道菜真的很好吃”那么有分量。

sentences.en: So what does this discussion of food have to do with the exchange we heard at the beginning of this report?
sentences.zh: 那么，这些关于食物的讨论与我们在本报道开头听到的对话有什么关系呢？

sentences.en: Let's think back to the business conversation:
sentences.zh: 让我们回想一下那次商务对话：

sentences.en: A: I really like your plan!
sentences.zh: A：我真的很喜欢你的方案！

sentences.en: B: Yes, it's pretty good … but it needs a little revising.
sentences.zh: B：是的，相当不错……不过需要稍微修改一下。

sentences.en: A: Of course, you did a very good job, but you might need to consider a few more points.
sentences.zh: A：当然，你做得非常好，不过你可能需要再考虑几个问题。

sentences.en: B: Yes, it will probably be more effective if you highlight the staffing requirements and expand on the budget.
sentences.zh: B：是的，如果你强调人员配置要求并详细阐述预算，效果可能会更好。

sentences.en: You might notice that one of the speakers uses amplifiers such as really and very.
sentences.zh: 你可能注意到，其中一位说话者使用了“really”和“very”这样的强化词。

sentences.en: She is using these words to give more force to her statement.
sentences.zh: 她使用这些词是为了增强自己话语的力度。

sentences.en: She is probably more excited about the business plan.
sentences.zh: 她大概对这份商业计划更加兴奋。

sentences.en: The second speaker uses downtoners – the words pretty and probably, for example.
sentences.zh: 第二位说话者则使用了弱化词——例如“pretty”和“probably”。

sentences.en: So you might suspect that he is more guarded about the plan.
sentences.zh: 所以你可能会怀疑他对这个计划更加谨慎。

sentences.en: Maybe he has doubts that the new plan will be better.
sentences.zh: 也许他会怀疑新计划会不会更好。

sentences.en: The amplifiers and downtoners they use are also among the most common ones that you will hear in American English.
sentences.zh: 他们使用的放大器和降调器也是你在美式英语中最常听到的那些。

sentences.en: These words are useful in a number of settings.
sentences.zh: 这些词语在多种场合都很有用。

sentences.en: They are polite and acceptable in almost any situation.
sentences.zh: 它们几乎在任何情况下都显得礼貌且得体。

sentences.en: Remember this: the amplifiers and downtoners we have discussed today are common in conversation.
sentences.zh: 请记住这一点：我们今天讨论的放大器和降调器在对话中很常见。

sentences.en: Different amplifiers and downtoners are more common in writing.
sentences.zh: 不同的放大器和降调器在书面语中更为常见。

sentences.en: For example, you are more likely to read words such as indeed, certainly, or approximately than you are to hear them in everyday conversation.
sentences.zh: 例如，你更有可能在阅读中看到indeed、certainly或approximately这样的词，而不是在日常对话中听到它们。

sentences.en: If you use these amplifiers and downtoners in conversation, your speech will take on a very official sound.
sentences.zh: 如果你在对话中使用这些放大器和降调器，你的说话方式会显得非常正式。

sentences.en: While that might be a good idea in a formal presentation or speech, it might not be the best choice for an everyday conversation.
sentences.zh: 虽然这在正式演讲或发言中可能是个好主意，但对日常对话来说可能不是最佳选择。

sentences.en: Amplifiers and downtoners are not always necessary to use in a sentence.
sentences.zh: 放大器和降调器并不总是需要在句子中使用。

sentences.en: But when you see or hear them, you are getting information about the thoughts and feelings of another person.
sentences.zh: 但当你看到或听到它们时，你就获得了关于他人想法和情绪的信息。

sentences.en: You are learning about how strongly they feel about something.
sentences.zh: 你正在了解他们对某件事的感受有多强烈。

sentences.en: And that's the end of this really long report!
sentences.zh: 这就是这份超长报道的全部内容了！

sentences.en: I'm Jill Robbins.
sentences.zh: 我是吉尔·罗宾斯。

sentences.en: And I'm John Russell.
sentences.zh: 我是约翰·罗素。
